findings.title: The sibling shared-slug embedding row `openai` has the defect that T-IGX-036-X fixed for `ollama`: resolving it as an embedding provider returns the managed-retrieval integration
findings.evidence: logs/openai_sibling_probe_head.json (identical at 324d9dba3): row `openai` has categories [managed_retrieval, embedding_provider] and the factory create_openai_managed_retrieval; resolve(EMBEDDING_PROVIDER, 'openai') raises IntegrationConfigurationError without OPENAI_API_KEY and, with a placeholder key, TypeError 'returned OpenAIManagedRetrievalIntegration, expected EmbeddingProvider'. The openai register module uses the same augment_integration_contract_specs pattern as ollama and was not touched (code read). Only two rows of the full default catalog carry more than one category (ollama, openai); after the delta ollama resolves, openai still does not. T-IGX-036-X lists other providers as out of scope; the ebh_5 harness catalog covers embedding_provider only with ollama and hf (code read), so no test pins openai. The RAG runtime binder bind_embedding_provider does not use the catalog factory (code read), so the failure is on the generic resolve / resolve_from_profile / health path (integrations/_shared/health.py).
findings.impact: any profile that binds embedding_provider to openai and is resolved through the catalog (health checks, execution-bound resolution) fails; not a security issue; the defect class (one catalog row, factory of the owning category) is only half closed
findings.recommendation: orchestrator/operator decision: development is frozen on product paths, so a mirrored dispatch for openai would be a new product path and another pin; alternatively accept, record as debt for the domain audit IA-D3 and add a pinned test

findings.title: The new tests do not pin the `enabled` handling or the pass-through of keyword arguments of the dispatching factory: 4 of 11 non-equivalent mutants survive (12th is equivalent)
findings.evidence: logs/mutation_sample.stdout.txt (control green: 508 + 3 tests): killed M1 inverted condition, M2 revert of the fix, M3 always-embedding, M7 no wrapper registration, M8 registration without override, M10 model-serving routed to embedding, M12 harness without owning row. Survived: M4 embedding branch hard-wired to enabled=True, M5 default enabled=True, M6 enabled ignored, M9 non-embedding branch calls the owning factory without its keyword arguments; M11 (string comparison) is equivalent. A first run whose -k filter deselected most tests (logs/mutation_sample_first_run_k_filter_deselected_most_tests.stdout.txt) reported M3 and M10 as survivors and was superseded.
findings.impact: a later change could flip the fail-closed default (enabled=False) of the embedding integration or drop configuration of the model-serving category without a red test
findings.recommendation: test-only addition by the ticket owner (assert enabled default False and True pass-through; assert keyword arguments reach the owning factory); route to IA-D3; accept for the rebind

findings.title: In the embedding branch `enabled` is coerced with bool() and every other keyword (base_url, api_key, ...) is silently dropped; both are carried over from the pre-B-REG-P embedding factory
findings.evidence: logs/probes_head.json P2: enabled='false' gives enabled=True; base_url and api_key are ignored (config base_url stays None) although the config class declares base_url; create_ollama_embedding_provider at c3d5b7005^ did the same (code read). The integration is catalog-only (module docstring: runtime binding pending B3), builds no client, reads no environment and makes no network call; default endpoint: none (base_url None), default enabled False.
findings.impact: no new credential, tenant or endpoint handling; a string 'false' read from a profile would enable a catalog-only flag; a configured base_url is not forwarded
findings.recommendation: accept for the rebind; address together with the runtime binding (B3) in IA-D3

findings.title: The embedding registration is two catalog writes (augment, then wrapper re-registration); between them the row advertises the embedding category with the owning factory
findings.evidence: logs/probes_head.json P6: an observer called between the two writes sees categories [model_serving_runtime, embedding_provider] and resolve(EMBEDDING_PROVIDER, 'ollama') raises the old TypeError; afterwards it resolves. A 200-round concurrent soak (P7) did not hit the window (0 of 200), so it is narrow; the second write cannot fail (override=True, no I/O). The catalog revision generation and digest are unchanged versus 324d9dba3 (P4 and the rebootstrap probe: generation 201 / 205 in both).
findings.impact: bootstrap-time window only; the catalog otherwise treats registration as atomic (registry/test_catalog_atomic_registration_concurrency.py passes)
findings.recommendation: accept; a single-write form (wrap the factory before the one write) would remove the window if the file is touched again

findings.evidence: attribution_of_regression_failures.json: head and 324d9dba3 fail the same 222 ids in isolation (9 pass); the pin fails 218 of 229 existing ids. 210 are red at the pin as well (test_provider_runtime_cutover 92, test_provider_category_contract_migration 67, agent_distribution 30, the rest; plus duckdb-dependent ebh_5/ebh_7 tests), 12 are new since the pin (F-35 x10, F-41 x2), 9 fail only inside the long run. findings.recommendation: route the 210 to the owners of the integration provider tests; accept as attributed
